nom: The Ordinary Retinol 0.5% in Squalane, Intermediate Retinol Serum

segments.oily: Oily-skin reviewers are sharply divided: several say the formula sits on top, does not absorb, and triggered bad breakouts, with some explicitly not recommending it for oily skin; a comparable number, including one who calls her skin insanely oily, report the opposite, a matte, less shiny, less pigmented finish with smaller-looking pores and no new breakouts.
segments.dry: Reports on dry skin are mixed: one reviewer explicitly warns against it for dry skin after it left her with flaky patches, especially on the T-zone, and breakouts along the forehead and chin, while others with dry or dry-combination skin report no irritation and real improvement, including for acne.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers are split: one found the oil did not absorb into her skin at all and saw no benefit, while others, including ones who describe an oily- or dry-leaning combination, report it hydrating well and keeping their skin barrier calm.
segments.sensitive: Most sensitive-skin reviewers, including some who are also acne-prone or have eczema, report no irritation and real improvement; a smaller number report a bad reaction, ranging from mild extra irritation compared with their usual retinol to, in one severe case, pimples all over the face.
segments.mature: Reviewers in their late 40s through 60s are consistently positive, reporting smoother, firmer, more moisturized skin and, for several, visibly softer wrinkles.

concerns.aging: Reviewers, especially those in their late 40s and older, widely report smoother skin, softer fine lines and wrinkles, and a firmer, more youthful look; one reviewer flags that the product's anti-aging claim itself cannot really be judged after only a few weeks of use.
concerns.dehydration: Most reviewers, including some with oily skin, say it hydrates rather than dries out their skin and helps lock in moisture overnight; the exception is a reviewer who developed dry, flaky patches, particularly on her T-zone, and a couple of others who saw some flaking in the first week or two that settled down.
concerns.redness: A few reviewers report redness or burning, including one whose eyes, lips and cheeks suddenly reacted badly after years of trouble-free use, and another who developed itchy redness during initial use; others report never experiencing any redness, and one reviewer notes that mild redness or burning on first use is a normal, expected reaction to retinol rather than a sign of a problem.
concerns.blemishes: Reports are sharply split: several reviewers describe severe or prolonged breakouts, in some cases lasting well beyond the usual purging window and leaving skin worse than before they started; a comparable or larger number report the opposite, including several who say it cleared existing acne, acne scarring or clogged pores with no new breakouts, even on skin that normally reacts badly to actives.
concerns.barrier: One reviewer says the product broke her skin barrier and caused perioral dermatitis even with careful, gradual use; another, by contrast, specifically credits it with keeping her skin barrier calm and never causing redness or dry patches.
concerns.spots: Reviewers consistently report fading dark spots, hyperpigmentation, sun spots or melasma with regular use, several noting visible lightening within a few weeks; no reviewer in this set reports new spots forming.
concerns.oiliness: Several reviewers, including ones with oily or T-zone-oily skin, report a matte, less shiny complexion and smaller-looking pores with regular use; the formula itself is widely described as oily on application, which some reviewers found worked against them rather than helping control shine.

Must be refrigerated, easy to overlook
Short shelf life relative to bottle size

Helps smooth keratosis pilaris on the body

extraits.texte: Do not buy this product. It is to high a percentage of retinol and even using the sandwich method it broke my skin barrier and caused perioral dermatitis. I tried mroe than once to ensure which product was causing it and every time i used this it would cause perioral dermatitis. Get a .1-.3% do not get this 0.5% it will damage your skin.

I am a huge ordinary fan however this product needs to be fixed as someone who has combination skin. I'm lucky to be able to use most products. However, this product is so oily, and my skin did not seem to absorb the oil at all. I feel like because my skin cant absorb it I didn't get the benefits, I don't recommend this unless you have super dry skin even then it's just so messy. You also need to refrigerate it. Which I don't really like because I like to have my skin care accessible and it only lasts three months. I am switching to the emulsion formula which is a more creamy formula and I'm hoping this gets reformulated. I thought about returning this product but instead I just threw it away. I've never thrown a skincare product away. I am disappointed because this is such an affordable price point and I love that they have different percentages, but I'm hoping that the ordinary considers evolving this product into a more creamyformula or like a water-based type serum

extraits.titre: Don't use if you have dry skin!
extraits.texte: When I first used this product, I loved it. I would put it on during my night time face routine and I would notice in the morning, my face was covered in dry flakey skin, especially in my T-zone. Then around my forehead and chin area, I would break out. If you have dry, sensitive skin, I would recommend one of The Ordinary's water based products. Those work wonders for my skin!

extraits.titre: For those who have used retinol before
extraits.texte: I love love this retinol and its price point. A few notes after reading other reviews, it does not take much, I use maybe 1/4 of a dropper. Let it sit for a minute or two before putting on moisturizer. it is of course an oil based serum and will absorp slower than a traditional retinol cream. if you have sensitive skin, do not use on your eyelid/undereye and get a seperate eye retinol cream (I like the roc one). Do not be surprised if your acne gets worse at first, your skin probably needed a purge. Keep your routine simple and limit other actives at the same time especially vit c or salicylic acid. do not exfoliate the same night. Use it every other day at most when you start, less often if it is your first retinol. The formula is to die for if you use it properly, I never have any redness or dry patches with it. I have combo/oily skin and it is so hydrating and great at keeping my skin barrier happy. As always WEAR SPF!!!

I wanted to start incorporating retinol in my skincare, so I decided to start with a more cost effective option rather than jumping to a $100 product I may or may not like. I ended up loving this product! It's been about 5 weeks since first trying it, and my skin texture and appearance has improved a lot. Almost all of my dark spots are gone, my skin is brighter, and more even overall. I like how the retinol is half strength of other products, and the squalane allows for some moisture support. Niacinamide makes me break out, so the squalane is a nice combination and I have had no problems with a break out since using the product.

Previously I was using a retinol serum by Olay that was okay-ish with treating acne scars along with preventing new breakouts but I felt like there had to be a better product somewhere else...That's where this serum steps in! Since I am not exactly a stranger with retinol I decided the .5% would probably be safe formulation for me to try and I am so glad I did :) I have INSANELY oily skin but after waking up the next day after using this product my skin was almost completely matte but still felt so hydrated and soft. I also have not had a single breakout since using this serum and overall my skin just looks better! And it has only been 3 days since opening the bottle so I can't wait to see how my skin looks long term. (Hopefully this can help with my black/whiteheads too) With all that being said...Squalane is an excellent skincare ingredient for those who have oily skin and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. The product might feel oily upon initial application but it will dry down. Also if you have never tried retinol before and you experience burning or redness that does not mean there is something wrong with the product...that is just a common side effect of retinol so do your research before purchasing! Thank you to The Ordinary for creating my new favorite skincare product :)
This is making such a difference in my skin. I am in my 60s and this has helped with keeping my skin looking more healthy.
